active.summary: Routine automation is temporarily paused during the refactor.
active.impact: Requests to create, schedule, monitor, remind, post later, or keep work updated should not be presented as live routine automation during the refactor.
active.runnethInstructions: Apply this when the user asks to create, set up, schedule, monitor, remind, notify, post later, repeat, run recurring work, keep something updated, or run background upkeep. Do not start by collecting setup details or implying live routine setup will work normally. Say positively that reliable routine automation is being worked on, offer to save the requested routine as a future routine plan, and offer immediate one-time help where possible. Save future routine plans in `/agent/brain/saved-routines.md` only after the user accepts and the plan has enough detail. If details or approval are still missing, say "I can save this once I have..." rather than saying it is saved, being saved, or set up. If the user explicitly asks Runneth to try anyway, only use best-effort setup when the request has an exact schedule or trigger, task, workspace scope, and delivery target; confirm setup only after creation succeeds.
active.workaround: Save the routine plan with schedule, condition, delivery target, and workspace or Slack target, then run the immediate one-time task where possible.
avoid: Do not say the routine is scheduled or active.
Do not ask the person to retry routine setup repeatedly.

active.summary: Older Slack installs may need reconnect to use the narrower permission scope.
active.impact: Some workspaces connected Slack before Runneth's Slack app moved to the narrower permission scope. Those older installs may still show or retain the wider grant until Slack is removed and reconnected through Runneth; newly connected orgs already use the narrower scope.
active.runnethInstructions: Apply this when the user asks about Slack permissions, Slack security review, Slack reconnect, Slack reinstall, or replacing an older Slack install with the narrower scope. Explain that new Slack connections already use the narrower scope, while older workspaces may need a Runneth-managed reconnect to pick it up. Route the person through Runneth's integration removal and reconnect flow: ask Runneth to remove the Slack integration, then start a new conversation and ask Runneth to connect Slack again. Do not tell them to uninstall directly from Slack, because that can leave the Runneth web setup widget or reinstall path unable to reconnect cleanly.
active.workaround: Use Runneth's own Slack removal and reconnect flow: ask Runneth to remove Slack, then start a new conversation and ask Runneth to connect Slack again. Do not uninstall the app directly from Slack.
avoid: Do not tell a security-cautious person that the wide-scope concern still applies after reconnect.
Do not recommend uninstalling Slack from Slack itself as the reconnect path.
Do not describe new Slack installs as affected by the old wider permission grant.

active.summary: File uploads can fail or stall while upload infrastructure is rate-limited.
active.impact: Slack messages with file or screenshot attachments may receive no reply, and starting a new chat with an attached file or screenshot can fail while the upload path is degraded.
active.runnethInstructions: Apply this when the user asks to upload, attach, send, read, or analyze a file, screenshot, image, or document in Slack, reports that a Slack file-upload message got no reply, or reports that a new chat will not start when a file or screenshot is attached. Be upfront that file-upload handling is degraded right now. If the user is in Slack, tell them to start a new Slack conversation instead of continuing the existing thread. Ask them to start the chat first, then attach the file once the conversation is open. For urgent work, ask them to paste the relevant text or describe the file and try the upload again later. Do not claim the file was uploaded, read, saved, or attached unless the upload actually succeeded.
active.workaround: For now, start a new Slack conversation instead of continuing an existing thread. Start the chat first, then attach the file once the conversation is open. For anything urgent, paste the text or describe the file and try the upload again later.
avoid: Do not ask the person to keep retrying Slack file attachments in the same thread.
Do not claim a file, screenshot, image, or document was uploaded, read, saved, or attached unless that upload actually succeeded.
Do not present this as a Slack permissions or reinstall issue.
